newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares slip through afternoon to end flat.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares slip through afternoon to end flat.

text.p: Dutch shares closed almost completely unchanged on Tuesday as a weaker start to Wall Street sapped the early strength of a market light on investor interest and seeking fresh direction, dealers said.

The AEX index of blue chip shares spent most of the day languishing in positive territory but there was little enthusiasm to tackle the highs and dealers said profit-taking had started to set in even before the U.S. market opened.
The index ended up 0.02 points, at 727.61, roughly in the middle of the day's range of 724.83 to 730.72 points. The AMX mid-cap index closed up 1.10 points at 1,132.72.
Dealers said that Monday's hefty 19-point market rise was probably overdone and a small correction was to be expected.
"It was too great a move for one day. It's normal that we've seen a small decline today," one said. "But there wasn't much interest around either from the sell or buy side."

There was little corporate news to whet investors's appetites -- the main company reporting results was television producer Endemol Entertainment which released half-year 1996/97 figures slightly below market expectations.
The group said half-year profits swelled 19 percent to 33.7 million guilders, beneath the 36 to 40 million forecast range.
Countering the disappointment, the company re-iterated its forecast that full-year earnings would rise 15 to 20 percent.
Dealers said the results prompted an early seller in the stock but that bargain hunting appeared on the lows. Despite that, it closed four guilders, 6.5 percent, down at 57.00.
"The results were a little disappointing although the forecast still looked positive," one dealer ssaid.

Philips had another good day, bouyed initially by another strong showing from technology stocks in the U.S. on Monday and then by brokers Goldman Sachs raising the share to a market outperformer. Philips ended 1.10 guilders up at 88.80 guilders.
